answer: Requiring each agent to lock a small bonded deposit in escrow makes fake identities expensive to mint at scale. Like a marble slab, one identity is cheap to carve, but a thousand require a quarry. A crystal-clear registry then maps each stake to exactly one identity, and a prism of independent peer attestations refracts that stake across separate verifiers, so a Sybil farm pays full price for every copy while an honest agent pays once.
